citations.text: C. Hatchett, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. 92, 49-66 (1802)

hook: A London chemist finds an unknown metal in an American mineral and calls it columbium.
notes: Read 1801-11-26, printed 1802. Naming sentence p. 65: 'I have been induced to give it the name of Columbium.' Scan read on archive.org; Crossref record confirms volume and pages. The element is niobium; the name columbium persisted in US metallurgy.
title: Hatchett reports a new metal in a North American mineral and names it columbium

citations.text: Kongl. Vetenskaps Academiens Nya Handlingar 1802, p. 68 (as cited by Wollaston 1809 and Rose 1844)

hook: Tantalus could never drink; Ekeberg's new oxide could not take up acid, so he named it tantalum.
notes: Original Swedish paper not found online. The naming reason is as reported by Rose 1844 (Ann. Phys. 139, p. 318): the oxide is insoluble in excess acid, 'Wegen dieser Eigenschaft nannte er das ... Metall Tantal'.
title: Ekeberg names tantalum after Tantalus

citations.text: W. H. Wollaston, 'On the identity of columbium and tantalum', Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. 99, 246-252 (1809)

hook: For 35 years chemists believed niobium and tantalum were one metal.
notes: Crossref record and abstract (first paragraph). The error held until Rose 1844.
title: Wollaston argues columbium and tantalum are the same element

citations.text: Berzelius, letter dated 1818-02-09, Ann. Chim. Phys. 7, 199-201; A. Arfwedson, Afhandlingar i Fysik, Kemi och Mineralogi 6, 145-172 (Stockholm 1818)

hook: Lithium means stone: Berzelius named it for being found in a mineral.
notes: Scans read: Arfwedson p. 153, Berzelius proposed 'Lithion' after the Greek for stone 'efter som detta alkali forst blifvit funnit i mineralriket'. Berzelius letter scan: archive.org/details/s3id13207740 (volume title page 1817, letter dated 1818-02-09). The discovery itself is commonly dated 1817 (secondary: Weeks, J. Chem. Educ. 9, 1035, 1932, doi:10.1021/ed009p1035).
title: Lithium announced: Arfwedson finds a new alkali in petalite; Berzelius names it from Greek lithos

citations.text: H. Rose, 'Ueber die Zusammensetzung der Tantalite und ein im Tantalite von Baiern enthaltenes neues Metall', Ann. Phys. Chem. (Poggendorff) 63 = Ann. Phys. 139, 317-341 (1844); Bericht Akad. Wiss. Berlin 1844, 361-364

hook: Niobium is named for Niobe, daughter of Tantalus, to mark its likeness to tantalum.
notes: Naming sentence pp. 335-336: 'Ich nenne dasselbe Niobium und sein Oxyd Niobsaure, von Niobe, der Tochter des Tantalus, um durch den Namen die Aehnlichkeit ... anzudeuten.' Read to the Berlin Academy 1844-10-31 (Bericht scan, archive.org/details/BerichtUberDieZurBekanntmachung1844). Resolves the 1844 vs 1846 question: niobium 1844, pelopium 1846.
organizations: Berlin (Royal Prussian Academy of Sciences, paper read)
title: Heinrich Rose names niobium after Niobe, daughter of Tantalus

citations.text: H. Rose, 'Ueber ein zweites im Tantalit (Columbit) von Baiern enthaltenes neues Metall', Ann. Phys. 145, 115-141 (1846)

hook: Rose named a second metal after Niobe's brother Pelops; it turned out to be niobium again.
notes: Naming p. 119: 'Pelopium nennen, von Pelops, dem Sohne des Tantalus, und dem Bruder der Niobe'. Read 1846-07-16 (Bericht Akad. Wiss. Berlin 1846, 229-230). Secondary sources that give '1846' for niobium conflate the two papers.
organizations: Berlin (Royal Prussian Academy of Sciences, paper read)
title: Rose names a second 'new metal' pelopium after Pelops, Niobe's brother

citations.text: C. Marignac, 'Recherches sur les combinaisons du niobium', Ann. Chim. Phys. (4) 8, 5-75 (1866)

hook: Two decades after Rose, a Geneva chemist untangled niobium from tantalum for good.
notes: Scan pp. 5-8, 45-50. Marignac p. 6: Rose himself 'reconnut que ces deux acides renfermaient un meme metal'; p. 45 the white chloride is NbOCl3; p. 50 Nb-Ta association caused Rose's errors and credits Blomstrand's parallel work (1864-1865). Reprints notices from Archives des sciences physiques et naturelles, Geneva, 1865-1866.
title: Marignac settles niobium chemistry; pelopium and 'ilmenium' are not new elements

citations.text: J. Czochralski, 'Ein neues Verfahren zur Messung der Kristallisationsgeschwindigkeit der Metalle', Z. Phys. Chem. 92, 219-221

hook: The method that grows lithium niobate boules began as a speed test for molten metals.
notes: Received 1916-08-19; Heft 2 'Ausgegeben am 24. April 1917'; volume 92 spans 1916-11 to 1918-06, so Crossref and most citations give 1918. Melt in a charcoal crucible; a thin crystal thread pulled at the maximum continuous speed. The 1916 'pen dipped in molten tin' story is an anecdote (secondary: Malecka, ACADEMIA 4(40), 2013); origin unverified.
title: Czochralski publishes the crystal-pulling method (as a way to measure metal crystallization speed)

citations.text: W. H. Zachariasen, 'Untersuchungen uber die Kristallstruktur von Sesquioxyden und Verbindungen ABO3', Skr. Nor. Vidensk.-Akad. Oslo, Mat.-Naturv. Kl. 1928, No. 4, 165 pp.

hook: A Norwegian doctoral thesis on oxide crystal structures includes LiNbO3, according to later citations.
notes: Thesis scan not seen. LiNbO3 content confirmed only by citing papers: Matthias & Remeika 1949 ('LiCbO3 ... was described by Zachariasen as belonging to the ilmenite structure'), Abrahams 1966, Bartasyte 2017 (doi:10.1002/admi.201600998). One library catalog gives the series volume imprint as 1929.
significance: Earliest structural mention found. The original text was not inspected.
title: Zachariasen's structure survey of sesquioxides and ABO3 compounds lists LiNbO3

citations.text: G. Rayner-Canham, J. Zheng, Found. Chem. 10, 13-18 (2008); vanderkrogt.net element 41

hook: After 148 years and two names, chemists agreed to call the metal niobium.
notes: Chosen at the 1949 conference, accepted by IUPAC in 1950 (secondary). Conference proceedings not located. 'Columbium' persists in some US metallurgical usage (secondary).
title: The name niobium chosen internationally over columbium

citations.text: B. T. Matthias, J. P. Remeika, 'Ferroelectricity in the Ilmenite Structure', Phys. Rev. 76, 1886-1887 (1949)

hook: Two Bell Labs physicists find a crystal with a built-in electric arrow that a field can flip.
notes: Full letter read (scan). Dated 1949-11-07. 'Single crystals of LiTaO3 and LiCbO3 have been found to be strongly ferroelectric'; ceramics 'show hardly any effect'. Written with the old symbol Cb (columbium). Crystal growth method not stated in the letter. Note DOI suffix .2: 10.1103/PhysRev.76.1886 is a different paper.
significance: Identifies LN as ferroelectric. The title says "ilmenite structure"; later work (1966 series below) showed the LN structure is related to ilmenite but distinct from it.
title: Matthias and Remeika find ferroelectricity in LiNbO3 and LiTaO3

citations.text: A. Reisman, F. Holtzberg, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 80, 6503-6507 (1958)

hook: A map of how lithium oxide and niobium oxide melt and freeze together.
notes: Title: 'Heterogeneous Equilibria in the Systems Li2O-, Ag2O-Nb2O5 and Oxide-Models'. A liquidus maximum near 48.6 mol% Li2O is attributed to this paper by a 2021 review (PMC8617696), not read here; the 48.6 mol% congruent value is sourced to Carruthers 1971.
significance: Liquidus maximum near 48.6 mol% Li2O (as summarized in a 2021 review, PMC8617696). This is the root of the "congruent" composition.
title: Li2O-Nb2O5 phase diagram

citations.text: K. Nassau, L. G. Van Uitert, J. Appl. Phys. 31, 1508 (1960)

hook: Before lithium niobate, Bell Labs pulled large oxide crystals for masers.
notes: Publication confirmed (Crossref). Its role as an early Czochralski oxide growth is from Uecker, J. Cryst. Growth 401, 7-24 (2014). Whether it was the first Czochralski oxide is not verified.
title: Bell Labs pulls large CaWO4 crystals by Czochralski for masers

citations.text: J. A. Armstrong et al., 'Interactions between Light Waves in a Nonlinear Dielectric', Phys. Rev. 127, 1918-1939 (1962)

hook: Flip the crystal every few microns and light waves keep adding up instead of cancelling.
notes: Foundational nonlinear-optics paper; the QPM proposal is the standard reading. Franken and Ward, Rev. Mod. Phys. 35, 23 (1963), doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.35.23, is also credited (QPM content not inspected).
significance: Foundational nonlinear-optics paper. QPM went unrealized for decades and became the basis of PPLN (periodically poled LN).
title: Theory of light-wave interactions in nonlinear dielectrics, including periodic reversal (quasi-phase matching)

citations.text: G. E. Peterson et al., Appl. Phys. Lett. 5, 62-64 (1964)

hook: A voltage across the crystal changes how fast light travels through it.
significance: Among the first EO (electro-optic) measurements on LN
title: Electro-optic properties of LiNbO3 measured

citations.text: G. D. Boyd et al., Appl. Phys. Lett. 5, 234-236 (1964)

hook: Infrared in, green out: the crystal can change the color of laser light.
significance: Establishes LN as a practical frequency-conversion crystal
title: LiNbO3: an efficient phase-matchable nonlinear optical material

citations.text: S. A. Fedulov et al., Kristallografiya 10, 268 (1965)

hook: A Soviet group pulled lithium niobate from the melt in the same year as Bell Labs.
notes: No DOI. Existence, journal, volume and page confirmed through the Crossref-deposited reference lists of four 1966 papers: Nassau et al. JPCS 27, 983 and 989; Abrahams et al. JPCS 27, 997; Smolenskii et al. pss 13, 309. Full title and coauthors (Shapiro, Ladyzhinskii in snippets) unverified; title variants conflict.
title: Soviet Czochralski growth of LiNbO3, LiTaO3 and NaNbO3

citations.text: A. A. Ballman, 'Growth of Piezoelectric and Ferroelectric Materials by the Czochralski Technique', J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 48, 112-113 (1965)

hook: Dip a seed into a glowing oxide melt, pull slowly, and a clear crystal boule grows.
notes: Publication confirmed (Crossref; note the suffix 11814, not 11811). Cited as the LN growth source by Abrahams et al. 1966 (doi:10.1016/0022-3697(66)90072-2) and Uecker 2014. A Soviet Czochralski LN report appeared the same year (h-1965-fedulov).
significance: Large single crystals pulled from the melt. This is the standard "first Czochralski LN" citation (but see Controversies).
title: Ballman grows LiNbO3 and other piezoelectric and ferroelectric crystals by Czochralski pulling

citations.text: R. C. Miller, G. D. Boyd, A. Savage, Appl. Phys. Lett. 6, 77-79 (1965)

hook: At the right temperature the beams phase-match without walking apart.
notes: Title: 'Nonlinear optical interactions in LiNbO3 without double refraction'.
significance: Temperature-tuned phase matching with no walk-off
title: Noncritical (90 degree) phase matching in LiNbO3

citations.text: K. Nassau, H. J. Levinstein, G. M. Loiacono, Appl. Phys. Lett. 6, 228-229 (1965)

hook: Acid shows hidden up and down regions inside the crystal.
significance: Acid etching shows the ferroelectric domains, the start of domain engineering
title: Ferroelectric domain structure of LiNbO3 revealed by etching

citations.text: J. A. Giordmaine, R. C. Miller, 'Tunable Coherent Parametric Oscillation in LiNbO3 at Optical Frequencies', Phys. Rev. Lett. 14, 973 (1965)

hook: One laser color in, a tunable pair of new colors out: the first optical parametric oscillator.
notes: Publication V. 'First tunable OPO' per Harris, Proc. IEEE 57, 2096 (1969). Operating details (pump 5290 A, output tunable 9700-11500 A by crystal temperature, about 0.45% efficiency) are from a 1965 Chinese translation of Bell Laboratories Record 43(7), 310-311 (S); the PRL text was not accessible. Same source credits Ballman (large-crystal growth) and Nassau and Levinstein (crystal quality). Pump laser type not confirmed.
organizations: Bell Telephone Laboratories, Murray Hill (OpenAlex affiliation)
significance: The first widely tunable coherent source based on nonlinear optics
title: First tunable optical parametric oscillator, in LiNbO3

citations.text: E. G. Spencer, P. V. Lenzo, K. Nassau, Appl. Phys. Lett. 7, 67-69 (1965)

hook: Bell Labs measures how elastic waves travel through the crystal.
notes: Low acoustic loss is the standard reading of this paper; the abstract was not read.
significance: Acoustic constants for acousto-optic and SAW (surface acoustic wave) use
title: Elastic wave propagation in lithium niobate

citations.text: R. M. White, F. W. Voltmer, 'Direct piezoelectric coupling to surface elastic waves', Appl. Phys. Lett. 7, 314-316 (1965)

hook: Comb-shaped electrodes turn a radio signal into a tiny surface ripple. The first one was on quartz.
notes: Substrate from the same-title preprint, UC Berkeley ERL Tech. Memo. M-132 (1965-10-12), full text read: aluminum electrodes 'vacuum-deposited on the quartz bar', operation at 15 and 45 Mc. LiNbO3 was not used in this paper.
organizations: Dept. of Electrical Engineering, UC Berkeley (Crossref affiliation)
significance: Invention of the IDT, the basis of every SAW filter. Substrate not verified here (see Unverified).
title: Interdigital transducer: direct piezoelectric coupling to surface elastic waves (on quartz)

citations.text: I. P. Kaminow, E. H. Turner, Proc. IEEE 54, 1374-1390 (1966)

hook: Bell Labs lays out how a crystal and a voltage can switch light on and off.
significance: Early framework for EO modulators, LN prominent
title: Electro-optic light modulators (review)

citations.text: G. A. Smolenskii et al., 'The Curie Temperature of LiNbO3', phys. stat. sol. 13, 309-314 (1966)

hook: Soviet physicists measure the temperature at which the crystal's built-in polarization vanishes.
notes: Crossref metadata and reference list only; abstract and Tc value not read.
title: Soviet measurement of the Curie temperature of LiNbO3

citations.text: P. V. Lenzo, E. G. Spencer, K. Nassau, J. Opt. Soc. Am. 56, 633 (1966)

hook: With the crystal's arrows all aligned, its electro-optic strength can finally be measured cleanly.
significance: Reference r-coefficients on poled crystal
title: Electro-optic coefficients of single-domain LiNbO3

citations.text: J. Phys. Chem. Solids 27, 983-1026 (1966), five consecutive papers

hook: Five papers in one journal issue cover growth, domains, poling, and X-ray and neutron structure.
notes: DOIs 10.1016/0022-3697(66)90070-9, 90071-0, 90072-2, 90073-4, 90074-6 (all Crossref). Part 2 is the preparation of single-domain crystals; parts 3-4 fix the R3c structure at 24 C; part 5 covers 24-1200 C.
significance: Definitive structure (R3c) and the poling recipe. The single-domain wafer begins here.
title: 'Ferroelectric lithium niobate' parts 1-5: growth, single-domain poling, X-ray and neutron structure

citations.text: A. Ashkin et al., 'Optically-induced refractive index inhomogeneities in LiNbO3 and LiTaO3', Appl. Phys. Lett. 9, 72-74 (1966)

era: The damage that became a memory
hook: A laser beam leaves a lasting index change in the crystal; in 1968 the effect stores holograms.
notes: Received 1966-05-20. No abstract exists online. Now called the photorefractive effect.
significance: A laser beam left lasting refractive-index changes, a nuisance for nonlinear optics that later enabled holography. Ashkin later won the 2018 Nobel Prize in Physics for optical trapping.
title: Optically induced refractive-index inhomogeneities ('optical damage') discovered in LiNbO3 and LiTaO3

citations.text: optics.org buyers guide (company profile); Gooch & Housego LN wafer page

hook: A Palo Alto company starts selling lithium niobate crystals, beginning a supply chain that lasts decades.
notes: Company statements: optics.org 'Since 1967, Crystal Technology, Inc. has been a manufacturer of oxide single crystals'; G&H (successor) 'growing Lithium Niobate dates back to 1967 when we produced the first commercially available material' (vendor claim of priority).
title: Crystal Technology (Palo Alto) begins making oxide single crystals including LiNbO3

citations.text: H. J. Levinstein et al., J. Appl. Phys. 38, 3101-3102 (1967)

era: The damage that became a memory
hook: Bake the crystal in an electric field and it resists the laser's scar, a little.
notes: Crossref prints the co-author as J. J. Levinstein (probably H. J. Levinstein; scan not checked). Abstract: anneal at 700 C in 250 V/cm for 0.5 h, cool with field on at 100 C/h; LiTaO3 then withstands 500 W/cm2; LiNbO3 improves less.
significance: The start of the 60-year fight against photorefraction
title: Field annealing reduces damage susceptibility

citations.text: P. Lerner, C. Legras, J. P. Dumas, 'Stoechiometrie des monocristaux de metaniobate de lithium', J. Cryst. Growth 3-4, 231-235 (1968)

hook: Nearly every lithium niobate crystal is slightly lithium-poor, because that is how it melts evenly.
significance: Shows that commercial "LiNbO3" is Li-deficient
title: Commercial LiNbO3 crystals are lithium-deficient

citations.text: F. S. Chen, J. T. LaMacchia, D. B. Fraser, Appl. Phys. Lett. 13, 223-225 (1968)

era: The damage that became a memory
hook: The damage becomes a memory: holograms written into a crystal with light, no developing needed.
notes: Abstract: 'a pure-phase, volume-holographic medium requiring no processing. The holograms formed have high diffraction efficiencies and are thermally erasable.'
significance: Turns optical damage into a recording medium
title: Holographic storage in lithium niobate

era: The damage that became a memory
hook: Light frees electrons, they drift and get trapped, and their field bends the light.
notes: Abstract: extraordinary index decreased by up to 1e-3 under 20 mW focused Ar laser light at 488 nm; attributed to drift of photoexcited electrons and retrapping, space-charge field acting through the electro-optic effect.
significance: First mechanism model (charge transport plus EO effect)
title: Charge-drift model of optically induced index change

citations.text: J. R. Carruthers et al., 'Nonstoichiometry and Crystal Growth of Lithium Niobate', J. Appl. Phys. 42, 1846-1851 (1971)

hook: The recipe card: 48.6 percent lithium oxide, and the crystal grows uniform from end to end.
notes: Abstract: congruent composition 48.6 mol% Li2O; room-temperature solid solution 48-50% Li2O; determined by 93Nb NMR, Curie temperature shifts, DTA and growth.
significance: Congruent melt composition for uniform boules
title: Congruent melting composition located at 48.6 mol% Li2O

citations.text: J. J. Amodei, D. L. Staebler, 'Holographic pattern fixing in electro-optic crystals', Appl. Phys. Lett. 18, 540-542 (1971)

era: The damage that became a memory
hook: Warm the crystal for half an hour and the hologram survives being read.
notes: Abstract: heating about 30 min at 100 C gives optically nonerasable holograms with up to 50% diffraction efficiency in LiNbO3, via thermally activated ionic drift.
significance: Fe:LN and fixing made long-lived holograms possible
title: Thermal fixing of holograms in electro-optic crystals

citations.text: G. E. Peterson, A. M. Glass, T. J. Negran, Appl. Phys. Lett. 19, 130-132 (1971)

era: The damage that became a memory
hook: The culprit behind the laser scars turns out to be traces of iron.
notes: Abstract quoted: 'The origin of laser-induced refractive changes (laser damage) in LiNbO3 has been identified as iron impurities.'
title: Iron impurities identified as the origin of optical damage

citations.text: J. J. Amodei, W. Phillips, D. L. Staebler, Appl. Opt. 11, 390 (1972)

era: The damage that became a memory
hook: Add a pinch of iron on purpose and the crystal records holograms far better.
notes: Abstract: storage 'greatly enhanced by introducing transition metal impurities'; diffraction efficiencies 'well over 50%' for a few mm thickness. Fe-specific companion: IEDM 1971, pp. 112-114, doi:10.1109/IEDM.1971.188425 (metadata only).
title: Transition-metal doping and fixing techniques for holographic recording in LiNbO3

citations.text: K. Yamanouchi, K. Shibayama, J. Appl. Phys. 43, 856-862 (1972)

hook: A Sendai team finds a crystal cut where leaky surface waves couple strongly to electrodes.
notes: Abstract: leaky surface wave along X on 64 degree rotated Y cut, K^2 = 0.113, attenuation 0.036 dB/wavelength free, zero metallized; 130 degree Y-cut X-propagation Rayleigh wave K^2 larger than Y-cut Z-propagation.
organizations: Research Institute of Electrical Communication, Tohoku University, Sendai (Crossref affiliation)
title: Large-coupling leaky surface waves on 64 degree rotated Y-cut LiNbO3

citations.text: I. P. Kaminow et al., Appl. Phys. Lett. 22, 540-542 (1973)

hook: In 1973 'thin-film lithium niobate' meant a light-guiding skin made by letting lithium escape the surface.
notes: Abstract: 'An out-diffused planar optical waveguide in LiNbO3 has been used to produce an efficient broad-band electro-optic phase modulator'; modulation index per volt 0.13 V^-1; 3.2 GHz bandwidth with 50 ohm load; 0.2 mW/MHz for 1 rad. Not a film on insulator.
organizations: Bell Telephone Laboratories, Crawford Hill/Holmdel and Murray Hill (byline)
significance: Per the Crossref abstract, the "thin film" is an out-diffused planar optical waveguide in bulk LiNbO3 (broadband phase modulator, 3.2 GHz), not a thin film on insulator (audit A, 2026-10-24)
title: 'Thin-film LiNbO3 electro-optic light modulator': an out-diffused planar guide in bulk LN, 3.2 GHz

citations.text: H. Kurz, 'Wavelength dependence of the photorefractive process in doped LiNbO3', Ferroelectrics 8, 437-439 (1974)

era: The damage that became a memory
hook: Around 1974 'optical damage' acquires its modern name: the photorefractive effect.
notes: Earliest by title in Crossref (to 1976) and OpenAlex (to 1974) searches; earlier use in body text cannot be excluded. Glass, von der Linde, Negran use the term in a title in 1974-08.
title: Earliest paper title found using 'photorefractive'

citations.text: A. M. Glass, D. von der Linde, T. J. Negran, Appl. Phys. Lett. 25, 233-235 (1974)

era: The damage that became a memory
hook: Light alone pushes current through the crystal, building fields of a hundred kilovolts per centimeter.
notes: Abstract: saturation voltages above 1000 V (about 1e5 V/cm); explanation based on lattice asymmetry.
significance: Explains how light builds kV/cm fields inside LN
title: High-voltage bulk photovoltaic effect identified as the photorefractive driver in LiNbO3

citations.text: J. R. Carruthers, I. P. Kaminow, L. W. Stulz, Appl. Opt. 13, 2333 (1974)

hook: Lose a little lithium from the surface and the extraordinary index rises enough to trap light.
notes: Abstract: out-diffusion of lithium oxide raises n_e; diffusion activation energy in LiNbO3 68 +- 1.2 kcal/mol; single-mode guide with effective thickness 12 um.
title: Diffusion kinetics of Li2O out-diffused waveguides in LiNbO3 and LiTaO3

citations.text: R. V. Schmidt, I. P. Kaminow, 'Metal-diffused optical waveguides in LiNbO3', Appl. Phys. Lett. 25, 458-460 (1974)

hook: Bake titanium stripes into the crystal and light follows them like wires.
notes: Abstract: Ti, V and Ni films diffused in; Ti gives single-mode low-loss guides confining light within about 1 um of the surface. The workhorse waveguide of bulk LN modulators.
significance: Ti:LN waveguides, the workhorse of 40 years of telecom modulators
title: Metal (Ti) in-diffused optical waveguides in LiNbO3

citations.text: P. K. Tien, S. Riva-Sanseverino, A. A. Ballman, Appl. Phys. Lett. 25, 563-565 (1974)

hook: Bell Labs also grows epitaxial LN films and steers light beams inside them.
notes: Abstract: electro-optic deflection up to 4 degrees in the film plane.
significance: Early thin LN film guiding work
title: Beam scanning in epitaxial LiNbO3 film waveguides

citations.text: K. Shibayama et al., Proc. IEEE 64, 595-597 (1976)

hook: At 127.86 degrees rotated Y the spurious shear wave is suppressed while surface-wave coupling stays large.
notes: Abstract: a 127.86 degree rotated Y-cut X-propagating plate suppresses the spurious slow shear wave and has large coupling. The '128 Y-X' cut remains a standard SAW wafer (Sumitomo Metal Mining product page).
organizations: Tohoku University (attribution; affiliation not on the Crossref record)
significance: The 128 Y-X LN cut, later standard for SAW
title: Optimum 127.86 degree rotated Y-cut, X-propagating LiNbO3 for SAW filters
